Name: Jeane Lui ("Jeje Sucesso")
Address: Avenida Raja Gabaglia, near Morro das Pedras
Description:
Jeane was shot in the street. The identity of her killer is not known, but one theory is that an argument at a funk dance the night before may have motivated the crime.

> “Jeane started out losing in life: black, trans, from the favelas. But she never stopped smiling and fighting. Life was not kind to her, as she was to life.” This is how Alexandre Silva Costa, president of the Cidade Jardim samba school, describes Jeane Lui, or “Jeje Sucesso” as she was known in the community. At 32 years old, the trans woman was brutally murdered in the early hours of this Sunday (5/1), victim of shots fired by a man, still unidentified, on Avenida Raja Gabáglia, in the Luxemburgo neighborhood, also in the Center- South Region.
> 
> An argument at a funk dance she attended the night before may have been the motivation for the crime. But before the tragic outcome, Jeane was a unique figure, beloved by the community and considered essential to the Cidade Jardim samba school — the biggest champion of the Belo Horizonte Carnival, where she had performed for almost a decade. The crime took place just a few meters from the samba school's court, a space that Jeane frequented and considered an extension of her home.
> 
> Jeane officially began her career at Cidade Jardim in 2016, but her connection with the samba school dates back much further. A resident of Morro do Papagaio, also in the South-Central Region of BH, she was a constant presence at community parties and events. For the school's president, Alexandre Silva Costa, the coexistence was natural. "She was a part of the family. Sometimes she would sleep over at my house. Jeje had a special affection for everything, she liked to see everything in its place. She was very organized and made sure to help, even when it wasn't t her responsibility," he recalls.
> 
> Alexandre also highlighted the lightness and good humor that marked Jeane's personality. "She called everyone 'success', she was very funny. That's how her nickname, Jeje Sucesso, came about. Wherever she was, she made everyone smile. People were enchanted by her," he told the Estado de Minas newspaper. 
> 
> A passion that, for those who knew Jeane closely, was described as a true mission, a life purpose. Skilled and dedicated, she was about to take over the production of costumes for the samba school and lead sewing workshops, which help raise funds for Cidade Jardim. Before that, she planned to participate in a 15-day intensive course in Espírito Santo, with the trip scheduled for this Tuesday (7/1). "Everything that was needed, even things that were beyond her control, she did. She was a person with a great spirit, always willing to help", recalls Alexandre.
> 
> The news of Jeane's death left everyone in the community shaken. The family was unable to inform the police whether she had been receiving threats. For Cidade Jardim, the loss is irreparable. "She was our 'success'. A person who transformed any environment into a lighter and more fun place", says Alexandre, who lives next to the school's court and heard the shots that ended his friend's life. "It was a cowardly thing to do. Hearing the shots and then finding out that it was her, it was devastating", he says.
> 
> An argument at a funk dance may have been the trigger for Jeane's murder. Known by everyone at the party, according to witnesses' reports to Estado de Minas , she got into a fight with a man, who has not yet been identified, and hours later was approached by two suspects.
> 
> A friend, who saw her on the other side of Raja Gabaglia Avenue, as she was leaving her house to go to the bakery, witnessed the crime. According to the report, the man approached with his gun already drawn and, taking advantage of the fact that Jeane's back was turned, fired the first shot. Even though she was lying on the ground, the shooter continued shooting before fleeing on a motorcycle with his accomplice.
> 
> Jeane was shot in the head. Near the body, the Military Police (PM) collected more than ten large-caliber ammunition shells on Sunday morning. As of this afternoon, the suspects had not yet been located. There are many witnesses, however, according to the military, most say they heard the shots, but did not see the shooter.

Name: Gabriela Araújo Santos
Description:
Gabriela went missing on 17th April 2023 after leaviing to go on a date. Her remains were found in November 2024 but she was not identified until January 2025.

*[Editor's note: The date given on the page is the date of Gabriela's burial, 6th January 2025]*

> The Civil Police of Goiás (PCGO) confirmed the location of the bones of Gabriela Araújo, a 26-year-old trans woman who had been missing since April 17, 2023. The remains were found in November of last year, in a wooded area in the América do Sul neighborhood, Novo Gama, in the Federal District, by a man who was looking for pequi in the region. With information from Metrópoles.
> 
> Gabriela disappeared after leaving her home in Gama, an administrative region of the Federal District, to meet someone she met on a dating app. According to her family, the last communication with Gabriela was a phone call on the day she disappeared, in which she said she was on a deserted, dark street and that her cell phone was running low. After that, there was no further news.
> 
> The family filed reports at both the 20th Police Station (Gama) and the Integrated Security Operations Center (Ciops) in Lunabel, Novo Gama. However, confirmation that the remains belonged to Gabriela only came after forensic examinations, which used DNA from two of the victim's sisters. The report indicated that the death was caused by multiple traumas to the chest caused by a sharp instrument, characterizing homicide.
> 
> Gabriela's remains were buried on January 6th, in the Gama cemetery. The family, who initially recognized the victim by her dental records, is now seeking answers about the circumstances of the crime and the identity of those responsible. The investigation is still under the responsibility of the PCGO.

Name: Natalia Santodomingo
Description:
Natalia's body was found in her home, which had also been robbed. According to her family she had received threats in the days leading up to her murder.

> The inhabitants of the municipality of Cajicá, located in the department of Cundinamarca and just a few minutes from the capital, are in shock after the discovery of the lifeless body of a trans woman inside her own home. Now her family faces the pain of her absence and more questions than answers in the face of the heinous crime.
>
> The woman, identified as Natalia Santo Domingo, was found in a room in her house located in the area known as Canelón.
> 
> According to the victim's sister, the last contact Natalia established was a call she made to her mother on January 9 at around 6:00 a.m. In this call, she stated that she had plans to go to the municipality of Tocancipá to see an apartment. 
>
> "Her room was locked, they went in and opened the room and found her dead. They locked her in with two little dogs that she had," said Diana Santo Domingo on the Citytv newscast, describing the moment of the discovery. 
>
> The family also stressed that days before the crime Natalia was receiving threats. In fact, the hypothesis being handled is that it could be a case of femicide.
>
> In addition, it is known that some belongings such as two cell phones and cash were missing from the property where the victim was found.
>
> The woman's relatives are asking the authorities to investigate the case thoroughly in order to find the person responsible for the crime and to ensure that justice is done. 
>
> "I sincerely hope that my sister's death will not go unpunished because she was killed in a very atrocious way, they were cruel to her and my sister was a very good person," she said. 

A candlelight vigil was held in Natalia's honour in the main square of the municipality on the Monday following her murder.

Name: Diany Ruiz
Description:
Diany was shot dead in a commercial premises by hitmen on a motorcycle.

> On the night of January 13, violence struck LGBTIQ+ people in Colombia again. Diany Ruiz, a trans man who was part of the Magdalena Diversa Foundation, was shot dead at the Ibiza commercial establishment, located in the Villarelis Tercera Escena neighborhood, commune 7, near the 07 de Abril neighborhood of the city of Barrancabermeja . The victim was intercepted by individuals traveling on a motorcycle, who fired several shots that caused serious injuries. Despite medical efforts to save his life, Diany Ruiz was transferred to a health center where he unfortunately died due to the severity of his injuries.
> 
> This is the sixth murder of an LGBTIQ+ person in Colombia in the first 14 days of 2025, according to the Human Rights Observatory of Caribe Afirmativo. This alarming figure reflects the deep dynamics of structural violence that affect our population and demonstrates the urgent need for effective measures to protect the lives and rights of LGBTIQ+ people throughout the country.
> 
> It is imperative that the national government, together with local authorities, implement effective policies and measures to stop this wave of violence. We reiterate the call for a real commitment to justice and respect for human rights, and we urgently call on civil society to collectively demand a country free of violence and discrimination for LGBTIQ+ people.
> 
> It is essential that a rigorous investigation be carried out with a human rights perspective, taking into account the specific risks faced by LGBTIQ+ people in their daily lives, ensuring that the motives for the crime are clarified and justice is achieved in Diany's case. 
> 
> Furthermore, it is urgent to prioritize measures that ensure protection and access to justice for victims of violence, implementing effective prevention strategies that address the particular realities and vulnerabilities of the LGBTIQ+ community, especially trans women, who are in a context of high exposure to violence and discrimination. The implementation of these measures is essential to safeguard the integrity and rights of this historically marginalized population.
> 
> Caribe Afirmativo condemns this new act of violence and express our most sincere condolences to the family, friends and loved ones of Diany Ruiz. This murder is a painful reminder of the lack of guarantees for the life and safety of LGBTIQ+ people in Colombia.

Name: Sarang Punekar
Description:
Sarang died by suicide. As well as being a passionate speaker and advocate for gender rights, she was the first transgender student to study at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

> Thirty-year-old Sarang Punekar, the first transgender student of Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU), died by suicide in Rajasthan on Wednesday. Her last rites were performed in Pune on Thursday.
> 
> In Rajasthan, she was living among the transgender community there and worked for them. “We had asked her to come back,” said Pune-based freelance writer Ashwini Satav, who worked with her for a long time.
> 
> Punekar was a strong supporter of the Ambedkarite movement and also raised her voice against NRC and CAA. “Sarang was brilliant in her analysis of caste and power hierarchy. As the first transgender student of the university, her very presence was a unique experience for us, both as academics as well as administrators,” Dr Anagha Tambe, head of the Department of Women’s Studies at SPPU which Punekar had joined in 2018, said. Tambe, while speaking to The Indian Express on Thursday at Punekar’s funeral, felt society at large failed to help Punekar realise her dreams.
> 
> Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sushma Andhare was among those who had gathered to bid farewell to Punekar, who had made a name for herself within a short time as a passionate speaker and advocate for gender rights and other causes. “As a student, Punekar brought about new perspectives to gender studies. She wanted to create knowledge and wanted to do original work about the language and customs of her community. It is our failure as a society that we could not support her dreams,” she said.
> 
> Punekar had worked as a regional coordinator, north Maharashtra, for Pune-headquartered NGO Samyak, which works for women and sexuality. Anand Pawar, executive director of the NGO, said she was first referred to Samyak as an intern but subsequently she was absorbed. “In the development sector it is always the norm to get transgender people to work in HIV prevention programmes. But she broke the stereotype and worked for abortion rights. As the coordinator she executed the project successfully,” he said.
> 
> In the course of her work, she had to coordinate with government officials, doctors and NGOs. The project got over in 2020 and Punekar decided to relocate to Rajasthan. “She said she wanted to be with the community there,” Pawar said.
> 
> Transgender poetess Disha Pinky Sheikh was her professor and personal friend. “She was a very strong voice. Her death marks the end of a very different kind of support for the community,” she said.

Name: Stephanie Francesca ("Steph")
Description:
Stephanie died by suicide.

> Stephanie Francesca was the woman I loved for eight years and fourteen days whilst she lived; she's also the woman I have continued to love since she died. 
> 
> On the 15th January 2025, Steph took her life in our home. She was 36 years old. 
> 
> She had only been blessed with being her true self for three years before the ignorant, hateful, and nonsensical voices in the world became too much for her to carry - and she didn't deserve to feel that way. No one - cis or trans - deserves to feel that way. To feel hated, simply for breathing. To feel reviled for finally feeling whole, finally feeling joy in being oneself, finally realising who you are and wanting to live your life quietly, in gentle contentment. 
> 
> She was a wonderful gardener. Our house was filled, across the year, with sprouts and flowers and colour - her basket of fire chilis, especially, were absolutely brilliant (if dangerous to those who dared use them). Her hair was the softest, curliest cascade, framing a flawless face with the deepest, darkest eyes. Her laugh was music, sometimes soft and sometimes the most raucous, filthiest thing you could imagine - but always, always contagious. Her smile could've lit cities. Her generosity was constant. She was intelligent, witty, stubborn, incredibly black and white. She was gentle, sharp, a constant curve of dualities and layers. She was human, she was flawed, but those things just made her more real, tangible, significant. And I loved her. 
> 
> Steph was so very many things, to people near and far, but most of all, she was loved. I will love her until I join her, wherever she is, and I'm fairly sure that my love is such that it'll continue even once my body is no longer here to carry it. 
> 
> Stephanie did not deserve to feel that the only option she could stand to live with was one where her life would have to end. She was not the first, and she won't be the last. 

Stephanie was a web developer, and her GitHub account (https://github.com/GrumpyPirate) includes 
an automated Minecraft texture pack compiler  named [Sphaxify](https://github.com/GrumpyPirate/Sphaxify). It also (sadly) includes her [suicide note](https://github.com/GrumpyPirate/suicide-note) - a thoughtful essay makes it very clear that the current climate of hostility and lack of care (including by the NHS) towards trans people had weighed heavily upon her.

Name: Blake Wava Quinlan
Description:
Blake passed away on Wednesday 22nd January. Ontario Provincial Police ruled their death to have been a suicide.

> Blake was a very passionate person dedicated to building community for those around them and worked hard with the Rural Ontario Community of Queer Youth to put on a series of care and wellness workshops and publish a zine of art and writing from rural 2SLGBTQIA+ youth from across the province, a number of whom were their friends. In the summers of their high school years they enjoyed attending 2SLGBTQIA+ summer camps. They were an incredible artist, worked doing theatre production in their hometown of Huntsville, Ontario which led them to pursuing their studies in Theatre Production at Toronto Metropolitan University. They were enrolled in their first year there at the time of their passing. They had a love for the forest, cooking, making art, poetry, and playing stardew valley.


Comments on their obituary posted by those who knew them paint a picture of a inspiring, friendly and creative person whose loss is an absolute tragedy.

> Blake was a wonderful person. We had known each other for a long time, and they inspired me and those around them to be unabashedly themselves. The world was lucky to have them for the period it did, and i will remember them forever. My deepest condolences to their friends and family.

> I worked with Blake - albeit briefly at Starbucks - but they were always fun and amusing. I am absolutely stunned to hear Blake's gone. I fully expected to see Blake at/involved with JC Superstar. I will miss seeing Blake's cheerful and friendly personality come to stock up on Fatface socks. My condolences to Blake's entire family over their loss.

> I was saddened to hear of the loss of such an intelligent, empathetic, creative, mature beyond years, warm and caring person. I taught Blake in grade 6, and they were the kind of student you never forget! Blake, may you shine just as brightly where you have landed, as you did here. Healing thoughts go to Blake’s family and many friends.

Name: Carolina
Description:
Carolina was from the municipality of Jericó and worked as a coffee picker. Her body was found with gunshot wounds and signs of torture.

> January 24, 2025. On January 23, 2025, in the municipality of Hispania, in the Vereda La Seca, Carolina, a trans woman from the municipality of Jericó, was found dead. She had lived in Andes for several years and worked as a coffee picker. According to preliminary information from the Judicial Investigation Section (SIJIN), the scene of the events was subject to a technical inspection and collection of evidence to help clarify the case. The body was found with her hands and feet tied, and showed signs of having been murdered with the use of a firearm.
> 
> This crime has raised concerns in the community and in human rights organizations, which have reiterated the need to implement more effective measures to guarantee the safety of the LGBTIQ+ population. This brings the total number of murders of LGBTIQ+ people in Antioquia to six, which is worrying due to the onslaught of violence and the lack of specific actions. It is clear that there is an urgent need to strengthen public policies to combat prejudice-based violence and ensure justice for the victims.
> 
> Carolina's case highlights the vulnerable situation faced by LGBTIQ+ people in rural areas of the country, where discrimination and lack of access to protection mechanisms increase the risks. Various social organizations have requested that this homicide be investigated with a differential approach and that those responsible be brought to justice.
> 
> We urgently call on local, departmental and national authorities to join forces to prevent violence and guarantee effective protection for this population group. We stand in solidarity with family and friends, hoping for justice in this case.

Name: Name Unknown
Description:
The victim was shot. No other information is known, but reportedlly they had been on the receiving end of threats.

> A 16-year-old trans teenager was shot dead in the early hours of Thursday (23), in the municipality of Primavera, in the Mata Sul region of Pernambuco. The body was found by residents in a rural area known as Engenho Amâncio.  
> 
> According to witnesses, the crime was expected because the victim had been receiving many threats via cell phone.  
> 
> The body was collected in the morning and sent to the Legal Medicine Institute (IML) in Palmares.  
> 
> In a statement, the Civil Police reported that an investigation has been opened and investigations will continue until the facts are fully elucidated.  
> 
> Last year, 105 trans people were killed in Brazil. Although the country recorded 14 fewer cases than in 2023, Brazil remains, for the 17th consecutive year, the country that kills the most trans people in the world.  
> 
> The data is from the Dossier: National Registry of Deaths of Trans People in Brazil in 2024: from the Expectation of Death to a Look at the Living Presence of Trans Students in Brazilian Basic Education, from Rede Trans Brasil. 
> 
> The majority of cases, 38%, were in the Northeast Region, which continues to be the one with the highest number of deaths of trans people since 2022. The Southeast Region appears in second place, with 33% of murders, followed by the Central -West, with 12.6% of deaths; the North, with 9.7%, and the South, with 4.9% of cases.
> 
> The majority of deaths recorded in Brazil are of trans women or transvestites, who account for 93.3% of the victims. The remaining victims, 6.7%, are trans men. The majority were between 26 and 35 years old (36.8%), were brown (36.5%) or black (26%) and were sex workers.

Name: Paula Nascimento Batista
Description:
Paula died after being run over by a man who had argued with her in a bar. Police arrested a 51 year-old man in connection with her death.

> In the early hours of last Saturday (25), a 51-year-old man was arrested after running over and killing Paula Nascimento Batista, a 26-year-old transgender woman. According to the Civil Police, the accident occurred after an argument between the suspect and the victim in a bar in Atalaia (about 40 km from Maringá).
> 
> Paula, who was a nurse and physiotherapy student, was at the scene with friends when she got into an argument with the suspect. The reason for the fight was not disclosed by the police.
> 
> The victim then decided to leave the bar on foot. At this point, she was hit by a vehicle driven by the same man she had argued with moments before.
> 
> Delegate Luiz Carlos Manica reported that there are indications that the crime may have been motivated by hate, considering that Paula was a trans woman.
> 
> “During the interrogation, he said he was drunk, had consumed alcohol and did not realize he had run over the victim. He believes he was run over, realized he had hit something, but didn't know he was the victim. We believe it was too much of a coincidence, but the facts still require further investigation,” he explains.
> 
> The Civil Police have opened an investigation into the case. The suspect is expected to be charged with intentional homicide and remains in custody while the investigation progresses.

Name: Elisa Rae Shupe
Description:
Elisa died by suicide outside Syracuse VA Medical Center. She was a trans veteran and at the time she passed her body was draped with the trans flag.

> Syracuse, N.Y. — A patient at Syracuse VA Medical Center died by an apparent suicide outside the top of the hospital's parking garage Monday.
> 
> Witnesses said the person was wrapped in a body-length transgender pride flag.
> 
> The transgender veteran [suicide method redacted], according to a notification the VA gave government officials. The veteran had been discharged from the VA’s inpatient psychiatry unit on Jan. 21, according to the notification.
> 
> Passers-by spotted the body at the garage next to the hospital and across the street from Syracuse University’s JMA Wireless Dome at about 11:15 a.m. Monday. That day, syracuse.com reported that a body had been found.
> 
> Anne C. Bellows, a professor of food studies, said she was walking back to her office on the top floor of the Falk College building when she and other SU faculty saw the body.
> 
> She said the person was wrapped in a body-length flag that was light pink, light blue and white — which she confirmed to be the trans flag.
> 
> The Syracuse VA officials declined to answer questions from Syracuse.com | The Post-Standard about the death. A VA spokesperson issued a statement that only confirmed a veteran had died at the VA Monday. It said officials will not provide more details, citing respect to the veteran’s family and an ongoing investigation.

In 2016 Eliza had became the first person in the United States to obtain legal recognition of a nonbinary gender.

In 2019 she publicly detransitioned, but in 2022 she published a statement reclaiming her trans identity and condemning the anti-trans movement's use of her story to push conversion therapy.

Name: Ayla Pereira dos Santos
Description:
Ayla and her (cisgender) friend Anna Clara Ramos Felipe were tortured and killed in what may have been a targeted execution.

> Two people were arrested during investigations into  the deaths of two young women, found in a wooded area and with signs of torture, in the city of Tangará da Serra, just over 240 km from the capital Cuiabá (MT), the Mato Grosso Civil Police reported this Thursday, 30. 
> 
> The bodies of Anna Clara Ramos Felipe and Ayla Pereira dos Santos, both 18 years old, were found at the back of a house in the Vila Nazaré neighborhood, on the night of Wednesday, the 29th. The victims showed signs of torture, such as burns on their bodies, and were gagged. 
> 
> According to authorities, the young women had been missing since Tuesday, the 28th, according to reports from family members. However, on Wednesday, the police received a report that they had been killed. 
> 
> During investigations to identify the suspects of the crime, the Civil Police arrived at the address of a 19-year-old woman, who was already being monitored in an operation against drug trafficking. The suspect told the team that she saw two young women tied up inside a house in the region and later witnessed that the bodies were taken to the back of the property, in a pasture area, indicating the location.
> 
> According to the Civil Police, Anna Clara's body was hidden in a bush and had burn marks on her back. Ayla, a young [trans woman], was buried in a shallow grave and also had burn marks. Both had gags in their mouths.
> 
> In the house near where the bodies were found, the team seized an iron bar, similar to the marks found on the two young women, as well as a shovel, a pickaxe, an excavator and portions of drugs. All the material was seized and sent for forensic analysis. 
> 
> After the arrest, the police also located a second suspect involved in the crime, a 34-year-old man, who was arrested and taken to the police station . Both suspects will be charged with the crime of concealing a corpse. The police are still searching for other suspects. 
> 
> Speaking to TV Centro América, police chief Igor Sasaki, who is responsible for the case, stated that the deaths were ordered by a criminal organization. However, the Civil Police are still investigating whether the victims were involved with factions.

Name: Aubrey Dameron
Description:
Aubrey was a two-spirit Cherokee trans woman who had been missing for nearly 6 years. Her remains were positively identified five days after being found on Friday 31st January.

> The Quapaw Nation Marshal Service sent out a media release on Wednesday, February 5, 2025, stating that on Wednesday, February 5, 2025, stating that on January 31, they responded to a call “regarding the discovery of human remains located near South 565 Road and East 30 Road, north of Commerce in rural Ottawa County, Oklahoma.” The area is about a 40-minute drive from where Aubrey was last seen. 
>
> The Oklahoma Medical Examiner’s Office responded to the scene and collected the remains, which were brought back to the office for further examination and identification. “Due to the condition of the remains, they appeared to have been at the location for an undetermined period of time,” the release states.
>
> Less than a week after the remains were located, they were positively identified as belonging to Aubrey Dameron. The Marshal Service stated that the family was notified of the identification, and they extended their “sincere condolences to Aubrey’s family and friends as the past six (6) long years of searching for Aubrey has come to an end.” 

Aubrey had gone missing from a small Oklahoma town on 9th March 2019. According to her family, her transition was not well received there:

> GROVE, Ok. — An Indigenous trans woman went missing from a small Oklahoma town in 2019 — her family believes her disappearance resulted from a hate crime. 
>
> News Nation Now reports that Aubrey Dameron, 25, was last seen leaving her family’s Grove, Oklahoma, home at 3:30 a.m. to meet an unnamed person in March of 2019. It has been nearly three years since she has last been seen, yet there are still no substantial leads in the search for Dameron.
>
> The family, a part of the Cherokee Nation, believes her gender identity had something to do with her disappearance. According to the news network, the family said her transition was not received kindly in the small town.
>
> “My immediate thought is that it’s a hate crime. That was my very first thing,” said her uncle.
>
> “Being in Grove. It’s not really diverse whatsoever,” [he] said. “There’s not really a lot of things that go on outside of the ordinary. And once there are, then it’s looked at as abnormal or weird or lacking, for lack of other words.”

Aubrey's death was subsequently ruled a homicide. The Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/MissingAubreyDameron was set up in her memory.

Name: Thayla da Costa Vieira
Description:
Thayla's body was found in a field. Her hands were tied and she had been stabbed and decapitated in a particularly brutal execution.

> In Sapezal, 473 km from Cuiabá, Thayla da Costa Vieira, a 25-year-old transgender woman, was found dead with signs of violence in a field near the municipal stadium this Friday (31).
> 
> The victim was found dead with injuries that point to extreme cruelty, with stab wounds, hands tied and a decapitated head next to the body.
> 
> Thayla had previously been detained on suspicion of drug trafficking, according to delegate Hugo Montenegro.
> 
> The Civil Police are investigating the case and there are still no suspects or known motive for the crime.
> 
> Politec (Official Expertise and Technical Identification) was on site and the body was released to the local funeral home.

Two suspects were arrested in April 2025.
